headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: CrewAI can write and egress broadly while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent framework with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI has a shared working-directory file surface and stdin/stdout, so if ai-engineering-hub outputs are copied into that workspace or parsed as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG/MCP-oriented repo, but no direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub outputs are pasted into CrewAI prompts or files
IF CrewAI tools parse file or stdout content as instructions
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts
Add a human review step before CrewAI consumes ai-engineering-hub output
Use explicit delimiters and instruction stripping for copied text

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed data and can read/write the host working directory while also using broad network egress to model providers and tools. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and its data handling is unverified, so a shared workspace could leak data from the pair into external calls. The exact leak path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same host working directory
IF CrewAI tools or model providers receive file contents from that directory
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory
Restrict CrewAI tool inputs to explicit allowlists
Turn off network access for runs that handle sensitive files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent framework that may also manipulate files or shared state when used in practice. Because ai-engineering-hub has no documented write surface here, the overlap is uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty escalates to medium when a plausible shared mutable workspace exists.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub is run in the same writable directory as CrewAI
IF both agents modify the same files or generated artifacts
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts
Snapshot the workspace before running either agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is an orchestration framework that can act on tool outputs, and ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG repo whose outputs may be treated as guidance. If CrewAI consumes ai-engineering-hub output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. No direct evidence shows automatic trust, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses ai-engineering-hub output as task input without validation
IF downstream tools execute actions based on that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action-taking tool call
Log and diff ai-engineering-hub outputs before reuse
Constrain CrewAI to read-only analysis mode
Add a second model or human reviewer for high-impact outputs

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed data and API keys, while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified open-source repo with no stated residency or retention controls. This creates a compliance gap only if regulated data is routed through the pair; the other agent is not cited because no specific residency or certification claim is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI runs
IF the deployment requires documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to the pair
Document retention and deletion handling before use
Keep API keys in a separate secret manager
Run a quick data-classification check before each session
